AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Although platelets play a key role in allergic inflammation in addition to their well-established role in hemostasis, the precise mechanisms of how platelets modulate allergic inflammation are not fully understood. IL-33 is an essential regulator of innate immune responses and allergic inflammation.

AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: We sought to determine the expression of IL-33 protein by platelets and its functional significance in airway inflammation.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: IL-33 protein in human platelets, the human megakaryocyte cell line MEG-01, and bone marrow-derived mouse megakaryocytes was detected by using Western blot analysis and fluorescent immunostaining. We examined the functional relevance of IL-33 protein in platelets by comparing platelet-intact and platelet-depleted groups in a murine model of IL-33-dependent airway eosinophilia elicited by intranasal administration of papain. We further compared the additive effect of administration of platelets derived from wild-type versus IL-33-deficient mice on the papain-induced eosinophilia.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Platelets and their progenitor cells, megakaryocytes, constitutively expressed IL-33 protein (31 kDa). Papain-induced IL-33-dependent airway eosinophilia in mice was significantly attenuated by platelet depletion. Conversely, concomitant administration of platelets derived from wild-type mice but not IL-33-deficient mice enhanced the papain-induced airway eosinophilia.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: Our novel findings suggest that platelets might be important cellular sources of IL-33 protein in vivo and that platelet-derived IL-33 might play a role in airway inflammation. Therefore platelets might become an attractive novel therapeutic target for asthma and probably allergic inflammation.
